title: AgentCC Gateway Admin Contract
description: Canonical backend-to-gateway admin API payload types.

Step.description: Agent step. Drives step-aware auto routing.

ContentMode.description: How much request content is kept. The most restrictive of org, key, request and global default wins.

ProviderMaxPrice.description: prompt and completion are USD per million tokens; request and image are USD per unit.

api_format.description: The upstream's wire protocol: openai, anthropic, gemini, bedrock, cohere or azure for model calls, or systemone for a structured-decision provider (TypeSafe, Perplexity Decider, a custom System One endpoint), with typesafe accepted as its alias. Empty lets the gateway infer it from the provider ID, which maps typesafe to systemone. A free string, so a format the gateway adds needs no contract change.

ToolCallGuardrailConfig.description: Guardrails on agent tool calls. checks names guardrail checks the org already configures.

AutoSelectorConfig.description: Optional LLM selector for ambiguous auto decisions. observe records its choice without acting on it.

AgentsEnvelopeDefaults.description: Default run envelope limits (P2). An unset limit is unbounded.

AgentsEnvelopeLoop.description: Loop guard (P2). action defaults to stop.

AgentsEnvelopesConfig.description: Run-tree envelopes (P2). Defaults: on_breach stop, soft_threshold 0.8, allow_downgrade false.

key_bindings.description: Administrative stable authenticated key ID to agent ID bindings; caller agent labels cannot select a cap bucket.

RolloutRoutingConfig.description: The candidate routing of a staged rollout: RoutingConfig without rollout. Keep the properties in step with RoutingConfig.

RolloutConfig.description: Staged rollout of a candidate policy. The gateway buckets traffic deterministically by sticky_by.

throttle_rpm.description: With action throttle: past the limit, the level admits this many requests a minute (default 1) and refuses the rest with 429 budget_throttled and Retry-After; under the limit it admits every request.

AdmissionCapRefusalMetadata.description: Value-free error.metadata for admission-cap refusals after a server-owned admission snapshot resolves, on every guarded route including stream start. Earlier policy, identity, binding, deadline or nonce validation errors may omit identity; an unactivated snapshot may report revision zero. Daily exhaustion retains HTTP 429, rate_limit_error and org_budget_exceeded; uncertain or unavailable admission state retains HTTP 503 and budget_state_unavailable. Unsupported execution retains call_cap_unenforceable. Only these typed admission refusals extend the Anthropic-shaped Messages envelope with code and metadata; run_budget_unenforceable (a Messages request under a run budget the endpoint cannot enforce, refused before dispatch) adds code only; other Messages errors retain type and message only. Never includes spend, limits, balances or monetary headers. A bucket-specific failure names that configured bucket; a ledger-wide failure names the first applicable daily bucket (agent before key), or the run policy if no daily bucket applies. Run-limit exhaustion is kind run only when the effective ceiling equals the administrative run limit (equal caller and policy ceilings enforce both); a tighter caller budget or persisted run ceiling and per-call caps keep their legacy errors, not admission identity. Run-state failures name the configured run policy, or the applicable daily policy when no run policy exists. Run-stop errors keep their legacy stop reason. Run policy identity is the administrative agent binding, falling back to the verified key ID, never the caller-supplied run ID.

policy_revision.description: Server-owned policy revision evaluated by this request, not a spend value. Zero identifies an unactivated policy; stale-policy refusals report the attempted revision.

AdmissionCapUSD.description: USD hard ceiling, rounded down to integer micros; absent is unset and explicit zero permits no positive-cost spend.

activated_at.description: Server-owned durable policy activation (RFC3339 UTC). Counts spend admitted since this instant, including BYOK, by UTC admission day; no history import. Cap edits never reset it.

policy_revision.description: Server-owned monotonic policy revision, positive even while disabled and distinct from the saved config version. Cap edits through update-config must send the last read revision as an atomic precondition; omission or 0 expects no saved policy. A stale revision returns 409 cap_policy_revision_conflict with the current policy_revision. Rollback assigns a fresh revision without resetting spend or activation time.

throttle_rpm.description: The org budget's throttle (org_limit with action throttle): past the limit, this many requests a minute (default 1); the rest get 429 budget_throttled and Retry-After.

fail_mode.description: Budget holds when budget state is unreachable (P1): closed (default) refuses with 503 budget_state_unavailable, open lets the request through unenforced.

no_max_tokens.description: A request with no max_tokens (P1): reserve_default (default) holds the estimate and records any overshoot, clamp forwards max_tokens equal to the estimate's output cap.

cooldown.description: A Go duration (e.g. 15m). After the rule fires it waits this long before it can fire again, while its condition holds. Empty or not a duration: 15m. 0s fires on every request past the threshold.

severity.description: Sent with every alert the rule fires (webhook payload severity, Slack text). Empty: warning.

trace_content.description: Full-content capture exports tool inputs and outputs to your organization's collector and masks known credential formats. Other sensitive content may still be exported. Off by default; only an organization Owner or Admin can enable it. Enabling and disabling are audited. Node body capture, full content mode and retention must also permit export.

PrivacyRetentionConfig.description: Retention TTLs for request logs and attempts, at most 36500 days (100 years; W2b integration, IC-4, so the daily purge cutoff never underflows). Ledger entries are never purged. store_bodies=false is read as content_mode=metadata.

MCPCredentialMode.description: How a server's upstream credential is resolved: none, the org's shared credential, the caller's own (per_user), RFC 8693 token exchange or ID-JAG (P3), or a vendor's per-end-user identity (vendor_end_user, GE MA4).

MCPCredentialState.description: A credential's state. M14 keeps the mode and marks the state when a credential lapses.

MCPCredentialSecretPart.description: PUSH-ONLY. One more secret part of a credential with more than one (AM-C20; MCPCredentialSecret.parts): its value and where it goes, by the rules of MCPCredentialSecret's own in and name.

MCPCredentialSecret.description: PUSH-ONLY. A static upstream secret assembled at push time by config_push (M14's assemble_for_push). It is never stored in an org config, returned by a GET or kept in config history. in and name say where the gateway places value (AM-C9); without them it goes in the header named by header (Authorization when unset), as before they existed. A credential with more than one secret part carries the others in parts (AM-C20).

in.description: Where value goes (AM-C9; connector-manifest/v1 credentialIn). header: the header named by name; header carries the same name, so a gateway that reads in but does not yet apply it (before CN7) places it the same way. query: the query parameter named by name. url_variable: the {name} variable in the path or query of the server's url, which only the push fills, so a secret never sets the origin. Absent: the header named by header. The gateway places the secret with a credential template (CN7); a placement it cannot apply exactly as stated (a name that is not its header, a query or url_variable name outside its pattern, a variable the url does not hold, a reserved header, or for a server with catalog_ref parts that differ from the catalog provider's) is refused at push by Django and at the admin PUT (400 mcp_credential_placement_unsupported, param naming the field), never sent elsewhere or in part (AM-C20). A managed tool credential goes in a header only.

name.description: The header, query parameter or URL variable that in names: an HTTP token of at most 64 characters, never a header the gateway sets itself; for query and url_variable also connector-manifest/v1's queryName or varName.

parts.description: The credential's other secret parts, for a vendor whose credential has more than one (AM-C20; Datadog's DD-API-KEY and DD-APPLICATION-KEY): in, name and value of this secret are its first part, and each entry is one more, placed by the same rules. At most 7, so a credential has at most the 8 parts connector-manifest/v1 allows. A single-part credential has no parts. Non-secret constant parts (Close's Close-Scope header) are never pushed: the gateway takes them from the catalog entry the server's catalog_ref names. A gateway that does not read parts would apply the first part alone, a partial credential, never a misplaced one. The gateway applies parts with its credential templates (CN7); a part it cannot place, or parts on a managed tool credential, are refused at push by Django and at the admin PUT (400 mcp_credential_placement_unsupported, param naming the field), never sent in part.

MCPIdentityBinding.description: Where a vendor_end_user server receives the end user's identity (GE MA4).

MCPServerCredential.description: The server's upstream credential. mode defaults to none and state to active.

expires_at.description: PUSH-ONLY. The vault's credential deadline; calls at or after it require authentication.

revision.description: PUSH-ONLY. The vault's grant revision for this server's shared static credential: every new or rotated secret has a larger one. The gateway admits the pushed secret only while its revision is newer than every revision a credential eviction (POST /-/mcp/credentials/purge with revision) has revoked for the org and server, on any gateway replica; a gateway with a distributed credential cache refuses a pushed secret that names none.

kind.description: shared only (CN24). oauth: the organization's one account is signed in over OAuth by an Owner or Admin, and the gateway fetches its token from the control plane when a call or a listing uses it (mcp-upstream-token-v1, the shared request), so no secret is pushed: a pushed secret on such a server is refused. credential_id and state name the signed-in account once there is one; until then the server has no tools. Absent: the credential the push carries.

MCPServerOAuthConfig.description: Upstream OAuth adapter (P4). adapter defaults to auto.

MCPToolLabel.description: Information-flow label of a server or tool (P9).

MCPServerOrgConfig.description: One upstream MCP server, keyed by a server id matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. Defaults: era auto, trusted_annotations false, timeout_ms 30000, tools_cache_ttl_seconds 300, propagate_depth false, enabled true. There is no private_network key: private egress is the operator list mcp.egress.private_allow (decision 39).

url.description: The upstream endpoint, used exactly. A save that changes its scheme, host or port while the server keeps a stored credential (a blank secret in update-mcp-server, an unchanged reference in update-config or POST org-configs) is refused with 400 mcp_credential_origin_changed: re-enter the credential or drop it (M14 IR-9, IC-R1-9). A path or query change keeps it.

transport.description: http, or sse for a 2024-11-05 upstream.

tools_cache_ttl.description: Legacy duration string (for example 5m). tools_cache_ttl_seconds wins when both are set.

forward_headers.description: Request headers forwarded upstream. authorization, cookie, x-api-key, proxy-authorization, mcp-session-id, mcp-protocol-version, x-agentcc-* and x-omega-* are refused (400 forward_header_refused), compared trimmed and case-folded; every name is an HTTP token.

toolkits.description: Operator-recorded toolkit slugs configured on this Composio session/server. Display hints only, labelled from server configuration; this does not configure the vendor session or grant access. Missing or unmatched configuration stays Other.

catalog_ref.description: The connector catalog record the server was added from (AM-C9): <app-id>/<provider-id>@<version>, with connector-manifest/v1's appId, providerId and semver patterns. Add-from-catalog (CN9) writes it, so the console can show an app as connected and an upgrade can follow the manifest. Absent on a server added by hand.

url_variables.description: The org's values for the catalog provider's org-scoped URL variables (connector-manifest/v1 transport.urlVariables and auth.oauth2.urlVariables), keyed by the manifest's varName, as add-from-catalog (CN9) filled them into url (AM-C9). A record only: the gateway never renders url from it, so url stays the one origin the credential origin rule checks (IC-R1-9). A secret URL variable is never here: it is the pushed credential.secret with in url_variable.

MCPAccessConfig.description: What a key bound to no virtual server, with no org default, may use (M10). default defaults to deny; M14's migration sets allow for orgs that had MCP servers before W3b.

MCPVirtualServerAccess.description: Who may use the virtual server. At most one virtual server per org sets default_for_org.

MCPApprovalConfig.description: Gateway-enforced approvals (M26). Defaults: require none, validity once, ttl_seconds 900. validity step binds an approval to the run, step and turn (P8).

MCPVirtualServerConfig.description: A virtual server, keyed by a slug matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$ and served at /mcp/v/{id}. Defaults: naming prefixed, mode direct, cache_scope private.

id.description: vs_<ULID>. Assigned by the control plane when the slug is created and never changed (400 vs_id_immutable).

members.description: Each member is a server id, fagi.<managed_id>, or <server_id>@<account_label> (P4).

MCPManagedToolCredential.description: The org's own credential for a fagi.* managed server (M14). Its presence means the org has had a credential, so a lapsed one never moves calls to managed unless fallback_to_managed is set.

expires_at.description: PUSH-ONLY. The vault's credential deadline; calls at or after it require authentication.

revision.description: PUSH-ONLY. The vault's grant revision for this server's shared static credential: every new or rotated secret has a larger one. The gateway admits the pushed secret only while its revision is newer than every revision a credential eviction (POST /-/mcp/credentials/purge with revision) has revoked for the org and server, on any gateway replica; a gateway with a distributed credential cache refuses a pushed secret that names none.

MCPManagedToolsConfig.description: The org's one managed opt-in for FutureAGI-supplied paid tools, MCP and REST capabilities alike (decisions 27 and 40). allow and deny take fagi.<id>/<tool> and <capability>/<vendor> globs. Defaults: enabled false, max_call_cost_usd unset, fallback_to_managed false, allow_user_tokens false.

MCPPinningConfig.description: Tool pinning (M20). Defaults: mode quarantine, new_tools quarantine, auto_baseline true. pins maps <server_id>/<tool> to the sha256 of the tool's canonical definition.

MCPScanningConfig.description: Description, argument and result scanning (M22). Defaults: descriptions warn, shadow true.

MCPFlowControlConfig.description: Run-level information-flow control (P9). Defaults: mode shadow, on_egress_after_taint approve.

MCPPolicyDefaultTier.description: Action per risk tier when no rule matches. Defaults: read_only allow, undeclared approve, destructive approve, destructive_prod deny.

MCPShapingConfig.description: Tool result shaping (P11). budget_bytes may not exceed the operator's mcp.max_result_bytes.

MCPOrgConfig.description: Org config mcp v2 (plan section 6.19). Every key is optional and its default keeps the pre-v2 behaviour.

MCPAdminStatus.description: mcp-admin-status-v1: GET /-/mcp/status?org_id=. enabled is the gateway's MCP switch, org_enabled the org's; every count covers the org's own servers only.

MCPToolPrice.description: The published managed price of a tool call, markup included.

MCPToolIdentity.description: Bounded display hint from the owning server's stored configuration, not vendor-asserted identity. Pipedream uses a single configured connection app; Composio uses a longest configured toolkit-prefix match, excluding meta/custom tools. Unknown, ambiguous or invalid configuration is other with empty slug/name and no source. No arbitrary upstream metadata is forwarded.

annotations.description: The upstream's MCP tool annotations, as sent.

MCPProbeAuth.description: A typed secret used for one probe only; never stored or logged (M14).

in.description: query: value is an api_key the probe sends as the query parameter named by name on every request to the url's origin, as the gateway places a catalog key there, and never in a header; no header is sent with it, and a url that already sets that parameter is refused. Absent: value goes in the header named by header (Authorization, as a bearer, when unset).

name.description: The query parameter, with in query (connector-manifest/v1 queryName).

MCPProbeRequest.description: POST /-/mcp/probe. At most one of credential_id and auth. The gateway refuses credential_id (400 invalid_probe_request): Django's probe view resolves it from the MCP credential vault and sends the credential inline as auth, and only where the org's active config sends that credential: a shared credential while its server's entry (mcp.servers.<id>.credential, or managed_tools.credentials.<fagi.id>) references it with state active and the probe url is that server's configured url (scheme, host, port, path and query compared); a per-user credential, which no config references by id, only by its own user and only to its server's configured url. Otherwise Django answers 400 mcp_probe_url_mismatch and the gateway is not called; a fagi.* credential cannot be probed yet (no managed catalog URL in Django). A typed auth may probe any url.

MCPProbeTool.description: One tool of a probe's listing (CN-ADD): its name, title and description as the upstream sent them (an empty string when one is not a string), and each of the upstream's four MCP behaviour hints (annotations.readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint) that it sent as a JSON boolean; a hint it left out, or sent as anything else, is absent. Never the tool's input or output schema. name is reported as sent, so a caller checks it against MCP's tool name rule before using it. revision is the tool's revision for pinning (M20): the hex sha256 of its canonical definition, the form tools_hash hashes the listing in, so an add pins each tool exactly as this listing saw it.

MCPProbeResult.description: mcp-probe-v1. Nothing is stored. tools_hash is the hex sha256 of the canonical tool list defined by the gateway's mcp.ToolsHash (M20 reuses it): each tool projected onto those of name, title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema and annotations it carries, as the upstream sent them, a duplicated key keeping its last value at every depth; JSON with no whitespace and object keys sorted by UTF-8 bytes at every depth; number literals byte for byte as written; encoding/json string escaping with HTML escaping off (U+2028 and U+2029 escaped, invalid UTF-8 as U+FFFD); the projections sorted by name (then by their bytes) and joined with commas inside brackets. It is neither Python's json.dumps(sort_keys=True) nor RFC 8785. error names why ok is false, for example egress_refused or not_mcp. tools (added for CN-ADD) is the same listing, one MCPProbeTool per tool in the order listed, present on every ok result (an empty array for no tools) and absent on a failed one; a gateway built before it sends no tools.

MCPRevision.description: mcp-revision-v1: a changed, new or colliding tool definition held by pinning (M20).

MCPApproval.description: mcp-approval-v1, bound to org, virtual server, tool, argument hash, run and principal (M26). Approvals are free.

MCPApprovalDecision.description: POST /-/mcp/approvals/{id}/decision. org_id must equal the org sealed in the approval id.

MCPOAuthKeysPush.description: mcp-oauth-keys-push-v1: PUT /-/mcp/oauth/keys. Public verification keys (JWK) of Django's authorization server; never a private key.

ManagedUpstreamKey.description: A per-org managed upstream key. Push-only: never stored in an org config and never returned by a read.

upstream_keys.description: Push-only. Assembled by config_push at push time; a save that contains it is rejected with secret_in_config.

ConfigMeta.description: Push-time metadata from AgentccOrgConfig. Never stored. The gateway's policy version is "v" + version.

ToolsCapabilityConfig.description: One capability's org settings (VC.1). Defaults: enabled false; providers empty (the price cards' default order); max_cost_usd_per_call unset. pinned options are developer-pinned and the model cannot override them.

ToolsPolicyConfig.description: Org capability policy (VC.1). Defaults: no_training_vendors_only false, zdr_required false, no region pin, no retention override. retention_override may only tighten a card's results_retention.

ToolsConfig.description: Org config tools v1 (plan section 6.36). There is no managed flag here: the managed opt-in is mcp.managed_tools. BYOK vendor credentials are providers.<vendor> entries.

IdentityIdPConfig.description: The org's identity provider for ID-JAG (P3). client_secret is PUSH-ONLY: assembled at push time by config_push (P3's delegated_grants.assemble_for_push), never stored in an org config or returned by a GET.

DelegatedGrant.description: A standing grant that lets an agent act for its grantor (P3). PUSH-ONLY, inside identity.delegated_grants.

IdentityConfig.description: Delegated identity (P3, plan section 6.30). require_human_sponsor defaults to false. idp.client_secret and delegated_grants are PUSH-ONLY.

delegated_grants.description: PUSH-ONLY. Active standing grants by grant id, assembled at push time; never stored in an org config.
